extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys) involved in filing and prosecuting patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing (pre-)publication content, timing, and filings for U.S. patent applications, including nonpublication requests, rescission, notice of foreign filing, EFS submission requirements, and how amendments/drawings/sequences are handled for patent application publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-stage amendments inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application publication of an application that has entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 may include amendments made during the international stage, such as: amendments under Article 34 and 19; rectifications; corrections of physical defects under PCT Rule 26; and an abstract rewritten by the International Searching Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These international-stage amendments can be included in the U.S. patent application publication when the application entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. No guarantee is given that any particular amendment will be included unless submitted per applicable procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement drawings timing for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant wants the publication to include drawings other than those submitted with the application, applicant may file the replacement drawings in sufficient time to be entered into the application file before four months prior to the projected publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot guarantee inclusion of the latest amendment. If applicant wants the publication to be based on an amended copy, applicant must supply a compliant copy via EFS within the EFS-Web Legal Framework deadlines (see separate EFS timing rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply amended application copy via EFS for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant wishes the patent application publication to be based upon a copy of the application as amended, applicant must supply such a copy via the electronic filing system (EFS) within one month of the mailing date of the first Office correspondence that includes a confirmation number for the application, or fourteen months of the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought under title 35, whichever is later (see 37 CFR 1.215(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will use the electronic copy provided by the applicant to create the publication. If the copy submitted under 37 CFR 1.215(c) does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish under 37 CFR 1.215(a). An untimely copy may be used only if received before the Office has started the publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing publication format
rubrics_metrics.description: Long nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences or large numbers of such sequences will only be published in electronic form on the USPTO sequence homepage as an ASCII text file; the patent application publication will include a statement that the application contains a lengthy sequence listing section and a hyperlink to the Web page containing the sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because long sequence listings are difficult to print in publications, the Office publishes them electronically and provides a hyperlink in the printed publication rather than printing the lengthy sequences inline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filing preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not file any preliminary amendment with the application. Submitting applications without any accompanying preliminary amendment reduces the processing required of the Office and helps ensure that patent application publications are printed correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date becomes part of the original disclosure under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) and will be included in the publication. If not in a format usable for publication, Office will issue a notice requiring resubmission in a usable format. Generally, a substitute specification (excluding claims) is required for preliminary amendments to the specification present on the filing date. Applicants should avoid filing a substitute specification with the application because the application size fee will be calculated based on the clean and marked-up versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate desired amendments into initial specification
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid preliminary amendments, applicants should incorporate any desired amendments into the text of the specification (including a new set of claims) at filing, even for continuations or divisionals; a new specification reflecting parent amendments may be submitted together with a copy of the oath/declaration from the previous application, provided no new matter is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific references to prior applications required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(a) for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 may be submitted in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) rather than in a preliminary amendment; if submitted in a preliminary amendment, a substitute specification is not required if only a benefit claim is added or amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for republication to correct publication errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of errors in the patent application publication and inclusion of desired amendments into the text of the originally-filed specification and drawings will occur only if applicant files a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a); they will not be corrected by the Office in a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1130 for details. A republication request is the procedure for correcting published errors rather than expecting the Office to silently fix errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and program listings printing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices, other than those containing sequence listings or certain tables, are not printed if they are contained on pages located after the claims. Computer program listings may be printed if included in the specification before the claims, but program listings provided on compact disc per 37 CFR 1.96(c) and 1.52(e) are not printed as part of the patent or patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple claim sets exist, pages after the first set of claims may be treated as appendices and not printed. Place critical material before the claims to ensure printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS compliance for amended application used in publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application submitted under 37 CFR 1.215(c) must comply with Office EFS requirements; if it does not, the Office will publish the application as provided in 37 CFR 1.215(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EFS copy is untimely but received before the Office starts the publication process, the Office may use the untimely copy. For further information see the Electronic Business Center on the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant information inclusion on publication (37 CFR 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent application is filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.46, the patent application publication will include the name of the assignee, person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention, or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest. This information must be provided on the Application Data Sheet (ADS) filed with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant information is corrected or updated under 37 CFR 1.46(c) after filing, the corrected info may be used if recognized by the Office of Data Management – Patent Publication Branch before technical preparation for publication has begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in applicant information treated as non-material mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in applicant information printed on the publication are not considered material mistakes by the Office under 37 CFR 1.211(b) (e.g., errors in the assignee’s name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such errors may only be corrected if applicant files a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.211(a). See MPEP § 1130.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee data submission requirements (post- and pre-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, if the applicant would like the assignee data to be published, the assignee data must be submitted on the ADS. For applications filed before that date, the assignee data may be provided on the application transmittal letter or ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee information on the transmittal letter or ADS does not substitute for compliance with any requirement to have an assignment recorded by the Office. If the assignee data is recorded only with the Assignment Division, it will not be published as part of the patent application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information errors correction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in assignee information printed on the publication are not considered material mistakes by the Office under 37 CFR 1.221(b) and may only be corrected if applicant files a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1130 for procedures to request republication to correct assignee errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirements for a nonpublication request (37 CFR 1.213)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request must: (1) be submitted with the application upon filing; (2) state conspicuously that the application is not to be published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); (3) contain a certification that the invention disclosed has not been and will not be the subject of an application filed in another country or under a multilateral international agreement that requires 18‑month publication; and (4) be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PTO/SB/35 (Nonpublication Request under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(i)) to ensure required language and conspicuousness. A request missing the statutory language will not be accepted. A nonconspicuous presentation (e.g., one paragraph among many with no highlighting) may be disregarded by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual inquiry requirement before certifying nonpublication (37 CFR 11.18(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making the certification in the nonpublication request, the person who signs must make an actual inquiry consistent with 37 CFR 11.18(b) to determine that (A) the U.S. application has not been the subject of a foreign or international application requiring 18‑month publication; and (B) the applicant’s intent at the time of filing is that the U.S. application will not be the subject of such a foreign or international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conditions must be satisfied to file a proper nonpublication request. The certification cannot be based on mere lack of knowledge, past tendencies, or statistical likelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuousness requirement for nonpublication request
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request must be stated in a conspicuous manner; providing the text as one paragraph among numerous other paragraphs with no highlighting is not conspicuous and may result in the Office assigning a publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/35 is recommended and reproduced in MPEP § 1135. Ensure the request is clearly presented and conspicuous in the application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement: nonpublication request must be filed upon filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request must be submitted with the application upon filing; this is a statutory requirement and cannot be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonpublication request filed later (for example, with a conversion under 37 CFR 1.53(c)(3) from provisional to nonprovisional) will not be accepted as filed upon the application filing date. The request must be included with the application papers and cannot be filed separately on the same date in a different package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper nonpublication certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonpublication request is improper (e.g., inconsistent with a priority claim or a prior foreign filing), the Office will not accept it and will assign a projected publication date. The applicant will be notified and given a non-extendable 30-day period to provide a satisfactory explanation; failure to do so will result in publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A representative making a false certification may violate 37 CFR 11.18(b) and other disciplinary rules. Applicants who discover an improper certification should promptly rescind the nonpublication request and note the improper nature of the original certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of a nonpublication request — form & content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may rescind a previously-filed nonpublication request at any time. A request to rescind must (1) identify the application, (2) state conspicuously that the nonpublication request is rescinded, and (3) be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). Form PTO/SB/36 (revision April 2001 or later) may be used to rescind and/or provide notice of foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rescission is filed before or on the date a counterpart foreign filing is made, the nonpublication request will be treated as never having been made. Rescission alone does not satisfy the separate statutory notice-of-foreign-filing requirement in all circumstances (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of foreign filing within 45 days required after filing foreign counterpart
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant who submitted a nonpublication request subsequently files a foreign or international application directed to the same invention in a country or under an agreement that requires 18‑month publication, the applicant must notify the USPTO of such filing no later than 45 days after the foreign filing date. Failure to timely notify the Office will result in abandonment of the U.S. application (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/36 may be used to provide both rescission and notice of foreign filing. A certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 will be given benefit for a notice of foreign filing. If the 45th day falls on a weekend or federal holiday, filing the next business day is timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission does not substitute for required notice of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere filing of a request to rescind a nonpublication request does not comply with the statutory notice requirement for foreign filing; applicants are strongly encouraged to provide a separate notice of foreign filing (Form PTO/SB/36) when rescinding in anticipation of filing a counterpart application abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the statute requires explicit notice of foreign filing within 45 days, rescission alone may not protect the U.S. application from abandonment if a foreign filing has occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office processing after rescission or notice of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a rescission of a nonpublication request or a notice of foreign filing, the Office will enter it into the Office Pre-Examination System to schedule the application for publication and will send a notice informing the applicant of the projected publication date. The application will be published promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the earliest effective filing date or as soon as practicable after mailing the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and correct submission of rescission/notice ensures scheduling for publication; failure to follow the specific process may delay publication or lead to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of unnecessary rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant should not rescind a nonpublication request or provide a notice of foreign filing unless a nonpublication request was actually made, because filing a rescission when one is not needed leads to waste of Office resources, may delay prosecution, and may result in a reduction to any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether a nonpublication request exists before submitting a rescission to avoid unintended negative consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment and revival limitations after improper nonpublication actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonpublication request was improper (e.g., because a prior foreign application was filed), the Office may publish the U.S. application rather than regard it as abandoned solely for having made the nonpublication request; a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137(a)/(f) is inappropriate and will be dismissed if filed in this situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not rely on petition-to-revive procedures to cure improper nonpublication certifications; instead, timely rescission or notice of foreign filing and compliance with statutory requirements is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use required USPTO forms (PTO/SB/35 and PTO/SB/36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/35 should be used for nonpublication requests under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(i) to ensure the proper statutory language and conspicuous presentation; Form PTO/SB/36 may be used to rescind a nonpublication request and to provide notice of foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are available from the USPTO website and are reproduced in MPEP § 1135. Using the official forms helps ensure statutory language and reduces risk of rejection for format or conspicuousness defects.
